name: logo-square-badge
story: A designer drew a lower third with a square badge, a dark background panel and two text layers for name and role, and saved it from Inkscape as Plain SVG.
idioms: the placed badge is a positioned <image id="image-badge" inkscape:label="Badge"> with x="214" y="770" width="160" height="160" and inline xlink:href base64 PNG data: URI
root attribute declarations xmlns:inkscape, xmlns:sodipodi, xmlns:svg, xmlns:xlink, fill="none", and inkscape:version="1.3 ..."
<sodipodi:namedview> element declaring document units, page dimensions, and current layer
inkscape:label beside every id on groups, shapes, images, and text layers to preserve human-readable operator names
-inkscape-font-specification in inline style attributes alongside standard font-family and font-weight
nested <tspan> elements with unique ids and sodipodi:role="line" carrying the rendered text
group layer container <g id="layer1" inkscape:label="Lower third" inkscape:groupmode="layer">
whyThisMatters: A 1:1 square badge (160x160) inside a lower third panel tests the interaction between placed raster logos and panel growth. It verifies that Inkscape's inkscape:label attributes correctly name both the swappable badge image and the text fields, that the panel background is identified as the growable rectangle, and that a square logo placed beside text remains anchored rather than being mistakenly offered as the expanding panel.
